items.summary: Version 1.2 (28 October 2026) adds a notice on the arithmetic precision of the split‑Gibbs runs (NOTICE_v1.2.md), with the check behind it (TF32_CHECK.md, tf32_check_files.zip). DP1’s split‑Gibbs runs used reduced‑precision (TF32) matrix products, which a later like‑for‑like check found shift that sampler’s estimates, while its predictions ran in full float32. The split‑Gibbs null result therefore has a further candidate explanation that DP1 cannot separate. DPS is unaffected. No file of earlier versions has changed. A pre-specified pilot testing whether a blindness-risk score computed before any target data are seen ranks the realised blindness (undetected and uncovered error) of diffusion-prior inference on real X-ray CT objects (2DeteCT) under simulated restricted access. Study DP-A: weak attenuation (F = 32,000), 240 errors × 20 bases. Study DP-B: bounded-reach control, 120 errors × 20 bases. Two samplers: split-Gibbs plug-and-play (primary) and diffusion posterior sampling (secondary). It follows the learned (VAE) pilot, arXiv:2610.28155 (reproducibility package doi:10.5281/zenodo.23392686). The analysis plan, decision rules and fixed result sentences were approved by the author, and predictions and calibration were committed by SHA-256 hash, before any trial. The plan was not lodged with an external registry, so the study is described as pre-specified; the files named PREREG_… are that plan (their names, and the word "pre-registered" inside the hashed plan and the dated log, are kept unchanged so that the recorded hashes still match). Version 1.1 (26 October 2026) adds a post-hoc check of the linear response used by the blindness-risk score, specified in a dated plan and approved before any computation (response_check_plan_v1.md, response_check.py, response_check_results.json, RESPONSE_CHECK.md). Under the plan’s pre-specified reading, the response was not adequate for either sampler in either study, so the null result for the learned score does not separate the learned prior from this approximation. The pre-specified results of version 1.0 are unchanged. README.md and freeze_log.txt are updated accordingly.
items.title: BLINDSET diffusion-prior blind-set pilot: analysis plan, code, frozen predictions, trial records and results

items.summary: This research investigates recurring inconsistencies, context retention failures, and ineffective error correction in long-term interactions between humans and large language models (LLMs). Using a retrospective dataset of 1,271 ChatGPT conversations comprising 26,949 user–assistant messages , the study examines how AI systems maintain conversational context, respond to corrections, follow established instructions, and represent the status of completed tasks. A systematic screening process identified 495 potential feedback signals across 192 conversations. From these, 26 anonymized case studies were assembled to examine observable behavioral patterns, including contradictory responses, task deviation, unsupported claims of completed actions, loss of previously established constraints, and repeated errors following user correction. The study introduces context-state mismatch as an operational framework for examining discrepancies between the conversational record and an AI assistant's subsequent responses or claims. It distinguishes directly observable failures from user-reported concerns and cases requiring further verification. The findings highlight important challenges in conversational reliability, transparency, instruction adherence, and long-horizon human–AI collaboration. The paper proposes evaluation methods involving correction retention, independent verification, and tool-action accountability to improve the reliability of future AI systems. As a single-user observational study, the research does not claim to establish population-wide failure rates or definitive internal causes. Instead, it contributes original longitudinal evidence and a reproducible framework for investigating persistent limitations in LLM-assisted workflows.
items.title: Context-State Mismatch and Repair Failures in Long-Horizon Human–LLM Interaction

items.summary: Test-time compute mechanisms, such as retries, confidence-based escalation and non-local routing, are conventionally deployed as black-box additions to trained models. They typically add forward passes or halting heads, but give no structural account of what the extra compute buys or what it costs against the model's stability guarantees. We therefore propose a theoretical and empirical framework for test-time compute on a Latent Dynamics Model used as the memory. When an encoder's latent state $(q,p)$ is advanced by a damped symplectic (velocity-Verlet) step of a learned Hamiltonian, every mechanism that expands access has an exact phase-volume Jacobian, a bounded energy change and an exact latch-transport law. We split reachability failures into escape failures and reach failures. A Lorentz squeeze resolves escape failures by injecting bounded, re-absorbable energy. A gated canonical translation (a one-step channel across $C_T$) resolves reach failures at $\detJ=1$ exactly. We verify this certificate stack on a designed analytic testbed. Reaching just beyond $C_T$ with the squeeze requires energy that grows quadratically in the excess distance. The gated channel's energy cost equals the potential difference between its endpoints, which is zero on the matched channel measured here, and so does not grow with distance in this testbed. An untrained state-replacing map annihilates phase volume and erases stored charge, while the gated channel transports it. On a learned physics-structured memory, we show calibrated compute rationing and evaluate the scaling limits of non-local routing against a physics-free baseline. The main contribution is the formalization and verification of the certificate stack, not benchmark performance.
items.title: Certified Access: Test-Time Compute on Conservative Physics-Structured AI Memory

items.summary: Packing a 3D volume into a token sequence is not merely long-sequence modeling. Once the volume is packed, sequence order no longer encodes the geometry of the sample---so a positional mechanism indexed by sequence position can learn the memory layout rather than the object. This is a general failure mode for attention over packed geometric data. We introduce PACK3D, a local-global attention operator that separates memory layout from attention geometry. PACK3D keeps local neighborhood attention exact, compresses only distant context into contiguous 3D block summaries, and indexes every query-key interaction with axial RoPE on true token-grid coordinates rather than packed positions. Because the rotation is applied before a block is summarized, the query-to-summary logit remains a weighted sum of query-relative 3D displacements; compressed global context therefore stays spatially interpretable after packing, instead of collapsing to anonymous pooled content. We measure the failure mode directly. On a controlled synthetic task---train on one packing, change only the memory order of the tokens, hold the physical labeling rule fixed---learned positional embeddings and packed-sequence RoPE solve the training layout perfectly yet collapse under Morton, block-contiguous, and random repacking, while axial grid-coordinate RoPE stays exact throughout. The same coordinate system carries to real data: on Allen WTC-11 hiPSC microscopy, PACK3D improves over a parameter-matched 3D U-Net on the 15-structure joint task and over a matched learned-position local-global baseline, with controls isolating the coordinate system, not encoder capacity, as the source of the gain. A fused Triton implementation matches windowed-attention latency at 65k tokens while supplying the long-range context windowing cannot---so the operator is not only correct but trainable at scale.
items.title: Geometry Matters in Packed 3D Attention

items.summary: Version 3 research revision. We study the part of a sensor field that remains covered after every failure in a prescribed downward-closed family. The model includes independent contact failures, weighted failure budgets and losses of entire fault domains. For a convex sensor cover with nerve N, we express the surviving region by a complex on the maximal faces of N: a collection of maximal faces is a simplex exactly when its common contact set cannot fail. This is a coverage formulation of classical nerve and Dowker duality, for which we give explicit comparison maps and prove naturality under increasing failure families. For n closed planar disks, all maximal nerve faces are witnessed by at most n^2 circle points. Exact rational sign tests consequently construct the full two-skeleton of the dual model without enumerating the original nerve or the coalition shadow. A separate Lipschitz margin theorem gives continuous coverage certificates for prescribed triangulated targets under the same failure rules. Recomputing five supplied fields completes the previously unfinished dense example: its two-fold covered region has Betti numbers (5,6), calculated from a dual complex with 130 vertices and independently checked boundary rank. The implementation, inputs, exact arithmetic conventions and verification records are supplied.
items.title: Sensor Coverage under Structured Failures: Dual Nerve Models and Exact Geometry

items.summary: Failures of deployed clinical artificial intelligence (AI) systems have often originated in how their training data were generated. Whether the programs that train the health AI workforce teach practitioners to examine data provenance is unknown. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the publicly advertised curricula of health AI education programs at U.S. universities, identified through a structured multisource web search between April and July 2026. Two investigators coded coverage of data provenance (structural, dataset limitations, or data management only), ethics, and sustainability; collaborative structure; technical prerequisites; and the disciplinary background and gender of named instructors. The primary outcome was provenance coverage at the structural or dataset-limitations level. Of 43 candidate entries, 36 programs at 25 institutional units in 21 universities were included. Ethics was covered by 29 programs (80.6%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 65.0 to 90.2), data provenance by 8 (22.2%; 95% CI, 11.7 to 38.1), and structural provenance by 6 (16.7%; 95% CI, 7.9 to 31.9). None of the seven master's degree programs met the primary outcome, and no program addressed sustainability. Eighteen programs included team-based work, but only 5 assembled teams across clinical and technical backgrounds. Of 92 named instructors, 76.1% came from computational disciplines and 3.3% from the social sciences or humanities; among the 51 whose gender could be determined, 66.7% were men. U.S. health AI education programs widely taught ethics but rarely taught how clinical data are produced. None addressed the environmental cost of computation, and most instructors came from computational disciplines.
items.title: Data Provenance and Ethics in the Curricula of U.S. Health AI Education Programs

items.summary: On PushT, our fixed action updater (1,505 parameters) solves 8 of 16 scenes reserved from our configuration selection. The comparison planners perform as follows: Selected Adam (7 tasks solved, total planning and encoding time 218.440s), adapted iCEM (2 tasks solved, total planning and encoding time 49.309s), released LePlanner (16 tasks solved, total planning and encoding time 5.652s). The total planning and encoding time for our action updater is 59.079s. Note that our action updater does not satisfy the task-cost criterion we fixed before evaluation. We also conduct another matched experiment where we only replay the first ten commands in each context and then allow the next solve 4, 8 or 12 updates (subsequent solves all get 8 updates). Among all 16 contexts (8 scene clusters), the 3 budgets get 9, 8 and 7 successes, respectively. Interestingly, the extra updates did not rescue any failing task in this experiment. All the changes in success/failure happen in one scene cluster, where we observe that the extra updates decrease the costs of the selected latent world-model trajectories for our updater, while the tasks that used to be successes become failures. The code, weights, evaluators, execution traces and cost accounting accompany the paper.
items.title: When More Planning Hurts: Learned Planners for World Models

items.summary: BIOLOGICAL SAMPLE MICROSCALE ISOLATION AND ANTI-CROSS-CONTAMINATION AT THE LIMIT Chinese Title / 中文書名:生物樣本微尺度隔離與防交叉污染極限 BIOLOGICAL SAMPLE MICROSCALE ISOLATION AND ANTI-CROSS-CONTAMINATION AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page, high-density English research monograph on whether microrobotic microscale isolation can improve sample-identity probability while limiting contact impulse, carryover and rare-sample loss. Its central claim is deliberately falsifiable. Under equal sample, time, energy, photon and analysis budgets, a preregistered isolation architecture should improve sample-identity probability without worsening contact impulse or carryover relative to commercial fluorescence-activated sorting at equal sample budget. A favorable result is rejected if downstream sensing creates the apparent improvement, rare targets silently disappear, purity rises by discarding difficult events, surface residue remains unresolved, or recovery improves while viability or molecular integrity fails. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates develop coverage entropy, calibrated identity posteriors, carryover transition models, complete material balance, rare-cell recovery and loss, purity, surface-memory decay, adsorption, desorption kinetics, hydrodynamic regime checks, contact impulse, shear dose, collision hazard, viability and molecular-integrity retention, blank limits, detection limits, witness information, uncertainty, equal-budget FACS effects, cross-site concordance and conjunctive release. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the book moves from identity authority and spatial coverage through contamination memory, microscale material closure, microrobotic contact physics, rare-cell accounting, decontamination, sample integrity, commercial FACS comparison and independent qualification. Two hundred Research Gates carry unique titles, questions, perturbations, rival accounts and evidence packets. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose genuinely different scientific objects, including contamination-memory ledgers, rare-cell censuses, adsorption compasses, waste-stream beacons, delayed-viability clocks and failure-preserving successor seeds. The work is explicitly nonclinical and hypothesis-generating. It does not claim clinical efficacy, regulatory approval or autonomous in-body deployment. Recovery improvement accompanied by failed viability or molecular integrity is a hard stop. No weighted score may compensate for broken identity, carryover beyond the preregistered ceiling or an unresolved material-balance residual. items.summary: Fight, flight, and relaxation describe bodily mobilisation and recovery but leave open how attention is selectively withheld or invested in discovery. This article examines ignoring and exploring as two modes of engagement whose neural and bodily organisation requires separate analysis. Ignoring reduces processing of particular information; exploring gathers information about something incompletely known. Evidence from distractor-suppression research indicates that ignoring is an organised, often learned and sometimes anticipatory form of neural selection. Research on curiosity, exploratory choice, and orienting relates exploration to motivated learning and arousal regulation, and shows that cardiac responses unfold in stages that distinguish information intake from preparation for action. The article separates attentional investment in an input from bodily mobilisation, which permits relaxed exploration, mobilised investigation, ignoring at ease, and ignoring under exertion. It distinguishes three ways of letting something pass (sensory filtering, nonreactivity to a noticed experience, and effortful suppression) that differ in what is recognised and in their bodily costs. Quiet readiness is defined in signal-detection terms as reduced interference from irrelevant inputs, preserved sensitivity to inputs whose relevance changes, a response criterion near its optimum, and bodily cost no greater than the task requires. Three failure profiles follow: rigid filtering (an overly conservative criterion), anxious vigilance (an overly liberal criterion at high cost), and distractible ease (weak suppression). Five hypotheses, each paired with a rival, are assigned to three staged studies. Implications for the M⁵ model of mindfulness are outlined. The framework is an agenda for testing, not a taxonomy of nervous-system states.
items.title: Ignoring and Exploring: Nervous System Engagement Beyond Fight, Flight, and Relaxation

items.summary: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.
items.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture

items.summary: The way software gets built is changing dramatically. AI agents now create pull requests, select dependencies, refactor codebases, interpret test failures, and execute infrastructure changes across the entire Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). AI agents are autonomous team members, but unlike human engineers, they are ephemeral - their reasoning, decisions, and tool calls vanish the moment the session ends. Modern Security incidents involving intent mismatch or injection are becoming increasingly common - forcing us to address AI Agents as an insider threat. No widely adopted standard yet enables agentic provenance and governance and its obvious that you can't hold an ephemeral process accountable. The git log was designed for human commits. It shows what changed. It does not show what an AI agent did, which model it used, which tools it called, or whether anyone was accountable for the outcome. Every governance framework, every audit trail, every compliance control in the SDLC was built around one assumption: a human made the decision. That assumption no longer holds. This shift introduces 3 main procedural problems (not addressing scale) - Supply-chain vector - The agentic coder is software, so it is a supply-chain security risk. Policy guardrails - How to ensure the agentic coder is compliant with the policies of the organization. Task-alignment - How to align the agentic coder on its tasks and goals. We introduce Agentic Process Evidence (APE), a signed, tamper-evident, machine-readable attestation of agentic processes, linking the sessions to their outcome (process-aware logging). APE enables Policy-as-Code control over the agentic processes, allowing for human in the loop only when it's needed. We support the in-toto style attestation framework, and the protocol is aligned with the relevant regulations
items.title: Agentic process evidence

items.summary: Multimodal large language models can recognize visual content yet struggle to reason reliably over it across multiple steps. In counting, a model may see all objects but lose track of which ones it has counted. We argue that such failures, commonly attributed to perception, reveal a reference gap: the failure to bind language to the relevant visual entities, regions, or locations. Motivated by the theory of visual routines, we test whether external references such as numbering can narrow this gap. We introduce ReGap-Bench, a paired benchmark of five visual reasoning tasks in which the scene, question, and answer are fixed and only the reference varies. Results show that task-matched references improve accuracy by up to 25\%, while mismatched references provide little benefit or even hurt performance. These findings identify the reference gap as a bottleneck distinct from visual perception and show that constructing task-appropriate visual references can serve as a training-free visual skill for improving multimodal reasoning.
items.title: Diagnosing the Reference Gap: What Visual Scaffolds Can and Cannot Fix in Multimodal Reasoning

items.summary: Borrowed Youth: Demographic Change and Multinational Location Advantage explains how national cohort succession and international recruitment become firm-specific location advantages over a production commitment. Home-linked relationships, recruitment shared across foreign affiliates and admission institutions determine attainable replacement labour. Version 3.33.0 clarifies the empirical bridge and journal exposition. The model-to-data mapping distinguishes accessible worker stocks and annual arrival flows from their discounted service values. Table 3 now leads with the main engineering-life comparison, followed by the accounting and common-support benchmarks. The country equal-pricing contrasts are expressed as conditional investment changes holding total measured international services fixed, with full covariance and uncertainty preserved. These transformations introduce no additional test, observation or regression. The discussion relates demographic succession to resource bundling, human-capital access and multinational portfolios. The exact AI declaration, including all figures, is preserved. Previously reported scientific results are preserved. The article supplies an explicit economic bridge from project value to expected investment allocation under stated choice, capital-size, duration and disclosure conditions. It distinguishes capital expenditure from accumulated assets, whose interpretation additionally depends on investment histories, depreciation and valuation changes. The retained capital-expenditure analysis uses the existing demographic construction and controls. There are 82 matched records from ten firms and 36 after fixed-effect support. The nuisance design has rank 33; the five focal regressors have rank three. Independent projection confirms this failure. No duration coefficient, interval or p-value is identified; the result is not a zero effect. The public module reconstructs the aggregate rank and supplies licensed rerun code without redistributing issuer rows. The existing engineering-life asset comparison remains: 317 allocations from 32 manufacturers in nine hosts, contrast -110.25 (95 percent interval -520.28 to 299.78; positive-direction p=0.724). Joint positive pricing and rotation are unestablished (p=0.763), and the familywise contradiction test does not reject (p=0.712). Existing Holm-adjusted block probabilities are 0.113, 0.085 and 0.656. All original estimates, covariance matrices, equations, formal results and six figures are preserved. These conditional associations do not identify recruitment-caused host choices. The held Nitra-Puebla appraisal supplies a EUR106-226 million residual strategic hurdle and 2,834 planned direct jobs. At a five-percent reference rate this is EUR2,959-6,308 per planned job-year. The retained frontier states the additional net productive service needed to cover an assigned share, excluding previously priced labour effects and without fitting a recruitment share. Cost-saving bounds distinguish fixed-life value improvement from a unique switch across lives. No new sources or observations were acquired. The manuscript has 9,920 counted words, a 172-word abstract and 23 full substantive pages before references; the main PDF has 41 pages and the appendix 137. Regression tables retain three-decimal probabilities, no significance stars and economic magnitudes. Counts include abstract, text, references and transparency; separately placed exhibits and the online appendix are excluded. Start with README.txt. Current article, appendix and complete LaTeX are directly downloadable. Three current verified ZIP blocks and nine frozen complementary archives reconstruct the exact 1,908-file replication tree with 1,907 checksum entries. Licensed WRDS rows are excluded; subscriber queries and public aggregate reconstruction are supplied. Third-party rights remain. Literature PDFs are linked rather than redistributed. ChatGPT and Codex (OpenAI) were used in October 2026 for coding h
items.title: Borrowed Youth: Demographic Change and Multinational Location Advantage

items.summary: Raw surface EMG (13 shoulder and elbow muscles) and isometric force/torque recordings (6 channels), sampled at 1 kHz, from three chronic stroke survivors who performed a virtual reaching task in immersive virtual reality with their most affected arm. The virtual cursor was driven either by the measured isometric force (force control) or by the force estimated from EMG (myoelectric control). In myoelectric control, a patient-tailored assistive-adaptive algorithm projected the participant's muscle pattern towards a healthy reference pattern, with an assistance level progressively reduced across blocks. For each participant the dataset contains one session of 9 to 16 blocks (376 trials in total): a maximum voluntary contraction block, force-control baseline blocks and myoelectric-control blocks at different assistance levels. Each trial file contains the raw EMG, forces and torques, the force driving the cursor, the task state, the trial events and the trial metadata (target direction, block, assistance level). A configuration file per participant describes the channels, the sensor calibration and the block settings. The data are pseudonymised. The files are MATLAB v7 MAT-files that can be read in MATLAB and in Python (scipy.io.loadmat). See README.md for the full description of the files and variables. These data support: Nocilli M., d'Avella A., Berger D.J. (2025). A novel approach to promote upper-limb motor recovery in stroke survivors using assistive myoelectric control and adaptive visual feedback in virtual reality. Front. Bioeng. Biotechnol. 13:1628679. https://doi.org/10.3389/fbioe.2025.1628679  Funding: Italian Ministry of Health, European Union - NextGenerationEU - NRRP M6C2 - Investment 2.1, project PNRR-POC-2022-12375705, CUP J83C22002060007.
items.title: Raw EMG and isometric force data from a pilot study of assistive myoelectric control with adaptive visual feedback in virtual reality in chronic stroke survivors

items.summary: Mathematical supervision for language models is typically flattened into isolated problem-solution pairs, discarding the curricular organization and evidential structure of the original sources. We introduce TOME-Math (Textbook-Oriented Mathematical Evidence), a large-scale corpus that converts 2,118 textbooks spanning the core areas of university-level mathematics subjects into approximately 380K structured proof-supervision records while preserving chapter order, proposition-proof links, dependency references, and source provenance. Leveraging these structural signals, we explore curriculum learning across multiple mathematical subjects and characterize scaling patterns with supervision volume and source breadth. At full scale, fine-tuning on TOME-Math raises the unweighted mean score across our held-out evaluations and established public benchmarks by 16.7 percentage points over the base model, while exceeding all three public instruction-data baselines evaluated in aggregate. Our findings highlight structured textbooks as both a scalable source of mathematical supervision and an empirical framework for studying the impact of data organization on mathematical reasoning. We will release the corpus to facilitate further research on structured mathematical supervision.
items.title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks

items.summary: Evaluating natural language explanations in recommender systems is essential for fostering user trust, transparency, and engagement. However, existing evaluation approaches like human evaluations, while accurate, are resource-intensive and impractical at the scale required by modern recommendation platforms. Also, automated methods using single-agent LLMs suffer from prompt sensitivity and inconsistent outputs. To address these challenges, we propose MAREval, a structured multi-agent framework for evaluating recommendation explanations using large language models. MAREval orchestrates (i) a planner agent that uses a novel Chain of Debate (CoD) prompting strategy to coordinate agent roles and enforce logically consistent evaluation plans; (ii) a moderator agent that regulates discussions by mitigating prompt drift; and (iii) an arbitrator agent that aggregates outputs from multiple evaluation rounds and (iv) a Monte Carlo sampling method, improving robustness and alignment with human judgment. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on both public (TopicalChat) and proprietary recommendation datasets, demonstrating that MAREval outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Comprehensive experiments on a public benchmark and a proprietary e-commerce dataset show that MAREval improves alignment with human judgments over strong singleand multi-agent baselines. Stability analyses indicate substantially lower variability across repeated trials. In a large human-annotation gate, MAREval meets production quality thresholds where prior evaluators fall short, and online A/B testing demonstrates statistically significant improvements in engagement and revenue metrics. These results establish MAREval as a scalable and reliable solution for human-aligned evaluation of recommendation explanations in real-world systems
items.title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations

items.summary: Supplementary material for the TGDK article "What the Oracle Knew". It contains the answer-generation and judging harness, the retrieval scorer, the benchmark fixtures and slices whose licences allow redistribution (LC-QuAD 2.0 CC BY 4.0, MetaQA CC BY 3.0, BRINK-family MIT; ComplexWebQuestions as identifiers only), and the frozen outputs of every condition, with md5 checksums. Every retrieval and generated-answer table of the article can be recomputed from these files without the Knowledge Navigator code; README.md gives the commands. The Knowledge Navigator code needed to re-run retrieval is deposited separately with restricted access. Version 1.3: adds the rebuilt MetaQA slice metaqa-kn-v1 (DECISIONS D14): the same 300 questions, with the relation path read from the official MetaQA question types instead of being inferred from the answers, and the full MetaQA knowledge base as A-Box. Includes the slice, the MetaQA files it is built from (question types, test questions, KB; CC BY 3.0) and its builder; the C_metaqa_v1 captures, revision summaries, generations and judgements for the six conditions and both generators (outputs/rev2, with MANIFEST.json and DIAGNOSTICS.md); and paper-side scripts (rev2_stats, agreement_v1, answer_bounds, metaqa_audit_sensitivity, diagnostics_to_json) checked by run_all.sh. In the article MetaQA v1 replaces v0 in Tables 3 to 8 and Figures 2 and 3; v0 is discussed only in Section 5.3 and stays in the archive for comparison. Every version 1.2 file and result is unchanged except the documentation (README, DATASETS, LICENSE-DATA, EXCLUDED, code/paper README), the harness (C_metaqa_v1 support; every earlier output reproduces byte for byte), run_all.sh (now 21 checks, Python 3.12 or later) and the md5 lists. Version 1.2: adds the linker-restricted baseline (Graph BFS restricted to the relations the production relation linker returned, DECISIONS D11) and the MetaQA vector-retrieval cell (D12), both at Knowledge Navigator commit 3e850458, with their captures, revision summaries, generations and judgements, the harness that recomputes them (KN_PAPER_REVISION=1) and three paper-side scripts (ci_rev1, linker_breakdown, answer_sensitivity) checked by run_all.sh. Used in Tables 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 and Sections 6.4, 6.5 and 7.1 of the article. The frozen version 1.1 results are unchanged. Correction: byte-identical reproduction needs Python 3.12 or later (version 1.1 stated 3.10+); run_all.sh now checks it. Version 1.1: adds code/paper (the statistics the article reports outside the two summary files, with frozen expected outputs and run_all.sh); keeps, for the ComplexWebQuestions runs, the per-case relation-linker error flag (no dataset text) so that Table 5 can count timeouts; removes a stray __pycache__ present in 1.0. Tables and frozen outputs are unchanged.
items.title: Supplementary material for "What the Oracle Knew": relation linking and generated answers in the Knowledge Navigator benchmark

items.summary: Objective pain assessment is challenging due to the inherently subjective and multidimensional nature of pain, compounded by intersubject variability and noise in naturalistic settings. These factors limit the development of reliable digital biomarkers for clinical decision support and remote monitoring. In this work, we propose a hybrid deep learning architecture that performs early fusion of single channel EEG band power streams with peripheral biosignals recorded by a wristband (electrodermal activity, photoplethysmography/BVP, triaxial accelerometry, and skin temperature). The model uses residual 1D CNN encoders to learn EEG representations and a multilayer perceptron to encode wearable features; the two embeddings are fused in a unified layer to produce predictions for four classes under a strict subject independent evaluation protocol. On PhysioPain, the proposed approach achieves 86.98% accuracy and 87.46% weighted F1, surpassing widely used machine learning baselines, while maintaining an average inference latency of 0.1495 ms per sample for real time operation. In addition to widely used machine learning baselines, we benchmark contemporary deep 1D CNN baselines for a fair comparison: the proposed model improves over 1D DenseNet by 4.49 percentage points in accuracy and 4.70 percentage points in weighted F1, and over 1D ResNet by 7.90 percentage points in accuracy and 7.93 percentage points in weighted F1. To our knowledge, this is the first study to perform subject independent multiclass classification of natural pain phenotypes with explicit handling of class imbalance by early fusion of MindWave EEG with Empatica E4 signals, representing a step toward generalizable and clinically useful digital biomarkers of pain.
items.title: Multimodal EEG–Wearable Integration for Generalizable Pain Classification

items.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly rely on persistent memory and inter-agent communication. These capabilities create privacy risks that extend beyond individual interactions: a release appropriate in isolation may become inappropriate when combined with information previously disclosed to a recipient or propagated to downstream agents along the planned workflow. Existing Contextual Integrity (CI) mechanisms for agentic systems typically rely on local judgments that assess each disclosure in isolation, with or without regard to the recipient's history, but do not account for how information propagates downstream. However, compliance at the current boundary does not guarantee appropriateness across the workflow. We introduce Task-Graph Contextual Integrity (TG-CI), to our knowledge the first task-graph-native formalization of Contextual Integrity for multi-agent systems. TG-CI represents a workflow as a Multi-Agent Task Graph (MATG) and extends CI from atomic transfers to stateful, graph-level information flows by jointly considering an item's intended propagation scope and recipients' evolving disclosure states. We operationalize TG-CI through propagation-scoped authorization under two complementary policies: Full-Scope, which requires admissibility across the complete downstream scope, and Auto-Region, which confines each item to its maximal admissible region using lightweight frontier gates. We further introduce MAPLE-Bench, a benchmark of 144 cases across four scenarios that jointly vary MATG topology, disclosure history, compromised-agent placement, and item-level privacy policies. In our primary experimental configuration, TG-CI reduces the mean unauthorized disclosure count by 85.8-94.1% relative to the Local-History CI baseline, while retaining 93.6-96.1% of the baseline's task accuracy, with the two enforcement policies providing complementary privacy--cost--utility trade-offs.
items.title: Judging Before Propagation: Task-Graph Contextual Integrity for Multi-Agent Privacy
